subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron tool policy, make cron inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep cron restrictions per-job only?
rationale: This changes a public configuration and security boundary, and the right default/precedence choice can affect existing cron jobs and message delivery behavior.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with compatibility-preserving defaults and explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Apply `tools.subagents.tools` to cron sessions too, reducing config surface but conflating two different runtime ownership boundaries.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Decline the global knob and document `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery-mode safeguards as the supported cron restriction path.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with compatibility-preserving defaults and explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`.

likelyOwner.reason: The previous review comment and adjacent security/config history make steipete the clearest product-decision routing candidate from the observed history.
